info.description:
Filings and company data for listed companies across the G20 and Europe. Send your API key in the `X-API-Key` header on every request. New here? Start with the [quickstart](https://financialfilings.com/developers/#quickstart).

**Credits.** Every call costs credits, and each endpoint below shows its price. `X-Credits-Charged` on the response says what a call cost, and `GET /usage/` shows the month so far. A free account gets a monthly allowance. Webhooks are an Enterprise feature. Pricing: https://financialfilings.com/developers/

**Rate limits.** Responses carry `X-RateLimit-Burst-Limit` (a rate such as `50/second`), `X-RateLimit-Monthly-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Monthly-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Monthly-Unit` (`requests` or `credits`). All four are strings and can be non-numeric (for example `Unlimited`); the last two are left out when they don't apply.

Retrieve a paginated list of companies.

parameters.name: cik
parameters.description: Filter by SEC Central Index Key (CIK). Accepts padded or bare (`CIK0000320193`, `0000320193` and `320193` are equivalent). The CIK is assigned by the SEC and survives corporate renames, mergers and ticker changes, so it is the stable key for reconciling a securities universe against our coverage.

parameters.name: countries
parameters.description: Filter by Company country ISO Alpha-2 code(s). Comma-separated for multiple values.

parameters.name: date_public_after
parameters.description: Companies last updated on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Granularity is one day (a Europe/Berlin date). For a full sync, seed the catalogue once first and partition that pass (by `countries=`, say), because offset paging stops at 50,000 rows, well short of the full catalogue. The few companies with no `date_public` yet are never returned by a date filter. A company updated while you page is re-dated, so following `next` can miss it; `date_public_cursor` cannot. De-duplicate by `id` and overlap windows by a day.

parameters.name: date_public_before
parameters.description: Companies last updated on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Granularity is one day (a Europe/Berlin date). For a full sync, seed the catalogue once first and partition that pass (by `countries=`, say), because offset paging stops at 50,000 rows, well short of the full catalogue. The few companies with no `date_public` yet are never returned by a date filter. A company updated while you page is re-dated, so following `next` can miss it; `date_public_cursor` cannot. De-duplicate by `id` and overlap windows by a day.

parameters.name: date_public_cursor
parameters.description: Resume a sync after the last company you received: `YYYY-MM-DD,<id>`, its `date_public` and `id`. Returns the companies after it in (`date_public`, `id`) order, up to and including yesterday, so today's changes arrive tomorrow. Requires `ordering=date_public`. Don't follow `next`: request page 1 again with the cursor set to the last company of each page, until a page comes back empty. Start with `<first date>,0`. A company updated mid-walk is re-dated to today and returned by a later walk, never skipped. Companies with no `date_public` are never returned.

parameters.name: ordering
parameters.description:
Sort field: `id`, `name`, `date_ipo`, `year_founded`, `country_iso__name`, `date_public` or `relevance`. Prefix with `-` for descending (e.g. `-name`).

`date_public` is the date the record last changed (Europe/Berlin). `-date_public` lists companies without one first; add `date_public_after` to leave those out.

With `search` or `ticker` and no `ordering`, results are ranked by relevance: exact ticker, exact name, name prefix, then fuzzy match, ties broken by filing volume. `relevance` only works with one of those two.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: A page number within the paginated result set.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of results to return per page.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Search across company name (including former names) and ticker symbol, and by LEI or ISIN from its start (a full code or a leading prefix such as `SE00128`). Case-insensitive, and accent-insensitive on the company name (`Hermes` matches the accented spelling). Multiple whitespace-separated terms are AND-combined (each term must match at least one of the searched fields); trailing legal forms such as `AB`, `AG`, `N.V.` or `plc` are ignored, so `EQT AB` finds `EQT`. Results are relevance-ranked unless an explicit `ordering` is supplied.

parameters.name: sector

parameters.name: sub_industry

parameters.name: ticker
parameters.description: Filter by stock Ticker symbol. Case-insensitive and separator-insensitive (`BRK.B`, `BRK-B` and `BRK B` are equivalent). Matches the company's primary ticker and its venue listings, so a secondary share class such as `GOOG` resolves to its issuer. A ticker held by several companies on different exchanges returns all of them (`count` above 1). To pin the exchange, append its ISO country code: `WDI.DE`, `1316.HK`. ISO codes, not Yahoo suffixes: `.PA`, `.SG`, `.L` and other Yahoo exchange codes are not read as a market.

Returns a company's cash dividends, one per dividend and share class, from the day the company announces them, so an upcoming dividend is listed before its ex-date. Each dividend carries its amount per share as declared, its ex, record and payment dates, and the filing that announced it. A later notice that moves a date updates the dividend and is listed in `date_changes`.

**Stated and derived dates.** Dates are as the company states them. Where a notice leaves the ex-date or record date out, it is computed from the market's settlement rule or from the company's own pattern on its past dividends, and listed with its rule in `derived_dates`; a later notice that states it replaces it.

**Amounts** are exact decimal strings, gross, per share, in the declared currency, as declared. `split_adjusted` carries the amount on today's share basis: divided by every split, reverse split and bonus issue in `/companies/{id}/splits/` that took effect after the notice stating the amount was published.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A unique integer value identifying this company.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only dividends in this status.

status.description: `upcoming` while its ex, record or payment date is today or later (or, with no date announced yet, for a year after it was announced); then `paid`. `cancelled` when the company withdrew it.

is_interest_on_equity.description: Brazil: interest on equity (juros sobre capital próprio).

share_class.description: `common`, `preferred`, or the class as the company names it.

instalment.description: `1/2`, `2/2` ... when the dividend is paid in instalments, each its own entry.

amount.description: Gross amount per share, as declared. Not adjusted for later splits: see `split_adjusted`.

derived_dates.description: Dates computed from a market or company rule instead of stated in a notice, each with its rule.

date_changes.description: Dates (and an amount restated after a split) a later notice changed, with the filing that changed them.

split_adjusted.description: The amount on today's share basis: divided (per-share figures) or multiplied (share counts) by `adjustment_factor`, the product of `ratio_new / ratio_old` of every split, reverse split and bonus issue in `/companies/{id}/splits/` that took effect after the filing the value was read from was published. A filing published after a split already states the new basis, so it is not adjusted again. `adjustment_factor` `1` and no `split_event_ids`: nothing to adjust. Rights issues and spin-offs are not adjusted. `value` is null, with `null_reason`, when the filing predates our split history (1990), when two events that cannot both be right would apply, when a split that applies is not served to you, near the record date of a split whose ex-date no notice states, for a period-end share count or book value per share with a split between the period end and the publication, or for a standalone quarter derived from filings published either side of a split.

derived_dates.ex_date: ex-date = 2 trading sessions before payment, the company's pattern on its past dividends
derived_dates.record_date: T+2 settlement: ex-date = 1 session before the record date

Returns a company's standardized income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement: `periods`, each holding its `statements`, each holding `line_items`. Use `depth` and `parent_code` on each line item to rebuild the statement hierarchy.

**One statement per period.** When several filings report the same fiscal year, period and statement type, one is selected. A filing with the company's own financials beats one without (such as an employee benefit plan's report), the company's reporting currency beats another currency, and a complete statement beats a fragment. Only then does the latest filing win. A selected statement in a currency other than the company's carries `currency_mismatch: true`.

**Currency is never converted.** `currency` is the currency the company presented in. A company that switches currency does not restate earlier years, so compare `currency.code` across periods before aggregating. A line item with its own `currency` comes from a dual-currency filing.

**Values.** `value` and `raw_value` are exact decimal strings: parse them with a decimal type. `raw_value` and `scale` are `null` when a figure was computed rather than read off the page. `confidence` is set only where an independent check re-derived the figure and agreed: `null` means unjudged, not low confidence. `source_page` is the page of the filing's PDF a value read from that PDF is printed on, `null` where it is not known.

**Source.** Each statement names its `source_filing`, with `document_url` and `viewer_url` to the document. The full `sources` list, including candidates that were not selected, is only returned to accounts with it enabled; `sources_masked` says which applies.

**Not the bulk dataset.** Comparative statements, restatements, quality flags and stable row ids are only in the S3 `line_items/` delivery. `is_comparative` says whether the selected figures came from a later report's prior-year column.

**Price and history.** One call costs the same however many periods or line items come back. An account limited to a rolling history window gets a `history_window` object; its `max_history_days` is the limit.

parameters.name: as_known_at
parameters.description: Values as we held them at this time (ISO-8601 datetime, e.g. `2026-10-20T12:00:00Z`; a datetime without an offset is UTC; a bare date `YYYY-MM-DD` means the end of that day in UTC). Each value we corrected or deleted since is served as it was then, a value first written since is left out, and each period's statement is then selected from those values under today's selection rules. Filings not yet released at that time are left out. Combines with `as_of`. History starts at 2026-10-19T17:05:18Z: an earlier time returns `400`; a future time is read as now. Statements are judged and ranked on what we held about them then (company, primary period, currency, filing type, title, release time): a statement moved to another company since is served and flagged `withdrawn_reason`; one moved to this company since is left out. Not reconstructed: period relabels, statements from filings removed since, and the `extraction` block, which is served as it is today. `updated_at` is capped at this time.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Filing-date cutoff (`YYYY-MM-DD`): only filings released on or before `as_of` are considered when picking the statement for each period. A filing whose own period had not ended by its release date is left out with all its statements: mostly that date is a placeholder, not when it was published. This is NOT a snapshot of the values we served on that date - figures are corrected in place, and a request with `as_of` returns today's version of each value from those filings. Use each line item's `updated_at` to see when a value last changed, and `as_known_at` for the values as we held them at a past time.

parameters.name: fiscal_period
parameters.description: Filter by fiscal period.

parameters.name: fiscal_year
parameters.description: Filter by exact fiscal year (e.g. `2024`).

parameters.name: fiscal_year_from
parameters.description: Fiscal year range start (inclusive).

parameters.name: fiscal_year_to
parameters.description: Fiscal year range end (inclusive).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A unique integer value identifying this company.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated. `revisions` adds a `revisions` list to every line item: each recorded change to that value, oldest first, with `old_value` -> `new_value` and a reason category. With `as_known_at`, only the changes up to that time. `preliminary` adds `preliminary_results`: the company's own preliminary figures, published before the report and labelled preliminary, never merged into `periods`. `as_reported` adds `as_reported` to a standardised total read straight from the filer's XBRL whose calculation tree ties: the face lines it is made of, as the filer tagged them. Not served with `as_known_at`. `standalone_quarters` adds `standalone_quarters`: one three-month period per fiscal quarter (H2 for half-year reporters), income statement and cash flow, derived from year-to-date interims where the company reports no three-month figure, each value flagged `reported`, `derived` or `derived_approx`, never merged into `periods`. `split_adjusted` adds `split_adjusted` to every per-share figure (EPS, book value per share) and share count, in `periods` and `standalone_quarters`: the value on today's share basis (or `as_of`'s), next to the unchanged as-reported `value`, with its `adjustment_factor` and the `split_event_ids` from `/companies/{id}/splits/` it applies. Recomputed on every request, so a split re-adjusts history the day it takes effect. Not served with `as_known_at`.

parameters.name: line_items
parameters.description: Comma-separated KPI codes to include (e.g. `revenue,ebitda,net_income_loss`). Omit to return all extracted line items. Statements with none of the requested codes are dropped. Unknown codes return `400`; see `/line-item-definitions/`.

parameters.name: statement_type
parameters.description: Filter to a single statement type.

template.description: The company's KPI template. Banks and insurers also get their template's own line items; see `templates` on /api/line-item-definitions/ for which items are meaningful for it.

sources_masked.description: True when your account does not have source identities unlocked. Then `sources` is omitted from every statement.

as_known_at.description: The instant values were reconstructed at, in UTC: a bare date is echoed as the end of that day, a future time as now.

currency_mismatch.description: True when this statement's currency differs from the company's modal reporting currency: the code held by more than 60% of the statements we serve for that company. When no code clears 60% (a genuinely dual-currency issuer, or one mid-transition) there is no modal currency and this is `false` on every statement, including the off-currency ones. A data-quality signal, not provenance, so it is returned even when `sources_masked` is true. It compares a statement against its company's history; it does not mean the statement itself mixes currencies.

accounting_standard.description: The accounting standard the statement was prepared under. National standards that are IFRS word for word (K-IFRS, TIFRS, HKFRS, SFRS(I), AASB, ...) are `IFRS`; ones with carve-outs or only converged (Ind AS, CAS, SAK, JMIS, any national GAAP) are `LOCAL_GAAP`. `UNKNOWN` when neither the filing nor its market says; null on statements not yet classified. See `accounting_standard_basis` for how it is known.

accounting_standard_basis.description: How `accounting_standard` is known. `xbrl_taxonomy`: read from the filing's own XBRL (a declared standard, or the standard taxonomy its facts are tagged in). `market_default`: not read from the filing; the standard listed companies in its home market must use for consolidated accounts, so an issuer with an exemption may differ. `filer_stated` and `document_stated` are reserved. Null when the standard is `UNKNOWN` or not yet classified.

statement_type.description: The KPI's home statement in the taxonomy, which can differ from the statement it was extracted onto. `SUP` appears here but is never a statement type.

value.description: Value in absolute units, as an exact decimal string, not a number. Parse with a decimal type; float loses precision at financial magnitudes. Null when the figure was withheld as unrecoverable.

raw_value.description: The figure as printed in the document, as an exact decimal string. When non-null, `value == raw_value * multiplier(scale)` to rounding (within 1% or 0.01). Null, together with `scale`, when `value` is null, when `value` was computed from other line items rather than read from the document (e.g. `net_debt` recomputed from the figures served beside it), or whenever `raw_value * scale` does not reproduce `value` (e.g. a value rescaled against the company's other filings), because then the printed figure is no longer the value's provenance. A printed total that is missing some of its components keeps its `raw_value`, because the printed figure is still its provenance.

scale.description: Reporting scale of `raw_value`. Withheld with it.

currency.description: The value's own currency code, which may differ from the statement's reporting currency for per-share figures. Null for ratios.

confidence.description: Confidence that this value is the figure the document states, or null where nothing has judged it. Non-null only where a second, independent check of the filing agreed with the extracted value; the number is that check's probability for the figure it picked. Null does not mean low confidence: it means unjudged, which is every value not yet checked and every value sent for review. Treat it as a filter, not a score: branch on non-null, do not compare nulls.

source_page.description: The 1-based page of the source filing's PDF the value is printed on, for a value read from the PDF rather than from XBRL. Null when it is not known: the document is not a PDF (XBRL, HTML), the value could not be placed on exactly one page, or the value served is computed or withheld rather than the printed figure (`raw_value` is then null too).

revisions.description: Present only with `include=revisions`: every recorded change to this value, oldest first (with `as_known_at`, up to that time). Empty when none was recorded. Recording started 2026-10-19T17:05:18Z; `pre_recording` entries are older corrections whose `changed_at` is approximate (the change happened at or before it).

op.description: `insert`: first written. `update`: corrected. `delete`: removed (it may be written again by a later `insert`). `pre_recording`: a correction from before recording started, approximate time.

old_value.description: `value` before the change; null on insert.

new_value.description: `value` after the change; null on delete. A change to another field of the value (its as-reported figure, currency or statement) has old_value == new_value.

reason.description: `extraction`: (re-)extraction from the document. `cleanup`: an automated rule-based correction. `repair`: a correction pass run by our team. `manual`: a hand edit. `unknown`: not recorded.

Returns a company's business-segment and geographic figures: revenue, operating profit and assets per segment and period, as the company tagged them in its XBRL filings. Available where companies tag their segment note in XBRL: US, Japan, Korea, Chile and India, and the few European companies that tag theirs.

Duplicate-company merges, oldest first.

When two records turn out to describe the same issuer we retire one and keep the other. The retired id disappears from the company list, so a warehouse built by incremental sync would otherwise keep the stale row forever. Poll this feed to reconcile.

**Poll `updated_at_from`, not `merged_at_from`.** Merges can be reversed, and a reversal edits the existing record in place rather than adding a new one: it moves `updated_at` but never `merged_at`. A `reversed_at` on a record you already ingested means the merge no longer holds and `shell_id` is a live company again.

Results are ordered by `merged_at` then `id`, so paging is stable even when a bulk merge writes several records in the same instant. Records are never deleted from this feed.

Covers merges recorded since 2026-06-29. Earlier cleanups predate this log and are not represented; companies removed by hard deletion rather than merge do not appear here either.

Match a list of your identifiers to our companies in one request.

Each row can carry any mix of `isin`, `lei`, `cik`, `ticker` and `name`, plus an optional `ref` that is echoed back so you can join results to your rows. Results come back in input order.

**Resolution order:** ISIN, LEI, CIK, ticker, venue ticker, name. The first hit wins, but every identifier you send is checked: if two point to different companies, the row is `ambiguous` with `identifier_conflict` and both in `candidates`.

**A name alone never returns `matched`.** A name-only row is at best `ambiguous`, with candidates to choose from.

**Tickers are checked against your `name`.** Tickers are reused across exchanges, so your name can pick the company that holds the ticker on another venue. A row matched only through a venue ticker is `ambiguous` + `name_disagrees` when the name disagrees, and `matched` + `security_listing_unverified` when you sent no name. If other companies hold the same ticker elsewhere, the row carries `multiple_tickers` and lists them in `candidates`. Add a country code (`WDI.DE`) to pin the exchange.

**Billing:** one request is one call, whatever the row count.

Up to 500 rows per request. Up to 50 rows that need a name lookup get one, within 25 seconds; rows resolved by an identifier don't count. Past either limit, a name-only row returns `not_covered` with `name_tier_skipped`, so split large name-heavy batches.

Retrieve the raw processed content of a single filing in Markdown format.

**Large filings.** An annual report can run to several hundred thousand tokens. Every response carries `X-Total-Chars`, the full document's length in characters. Pass `offset` and/or `limit` (characters) to read one window instead of the whole document; while characters remain after the window, the response also carries `X-Next-Offset`. To find the part you need first, use `GET /filings/{id}/markdown/search/?q=`. Each call, whole or windowed, is billed as one Markdown request. Through the MCP server, which pages large filings in chunks, a filing's Markdown is billed once per day.

Every line item a financial statement can contain. `depth` and `parent_code` give the statement hierarchy.

* `SUP` - Supplemental / Ratio

parameters.name: template

* `bank` - bank
* `insurer` - insurer

status.description:
`matched`: resolved to exactly one company. `matched_via_alias`: a name-only row whose name is a recorded former or alternative name of exactly one company; see `company`. `ambiguous`: several plausible companies, see `candidates`. `not_covered`: no company found.

* `matched` - Resolved to exactly one company
* `matched_via_alias` - Name is a recorded former or alternative name of exactly one company
* `ambiguous` - Several plausible companies; see candidates
* `not_covered` - No company found

resolved_via.description:
Which identifier produced the match. Null unless `status` is `matched`. Also null for `matched_via_alias`, where the name produced it.

* `isin` - ISIN
* `lei` - Legal Entity Identifier
* `cik` - SEC Central Index Key
* `ticker` - Primary ticker
* `security_listing` - Venue ticker via security listing

warnings.description: Stable codes qualifying the result. `no_identifiers`: the row carried nothing to match on. `identifier_conflict`: two identifiers on this row resolved to different companies; both are in `candidates`. `name_disagrees`: a ticker matched but the supplied name shares no distinguishing token with ours, so the match is not asserted. `multiple_tickers`: the ticker maps to more than one company. On an `ambiguous` result they are the `candidates`; on a `matched` result the company holds it as its primary ticker and the `candidates` hold it on other venues. `security_listing_unverified`: matched on a venue ticker with no name supplied, so the match could not be corroborated. This code covers two situations that cannot be told apart: the listing may be one of the known ticker collisions, or the ticker may since have been reassigned to a different issuer. Supplying `name` resolves the first but not the second. `name_tier_skipped`: the per-request name-lookup budget was exhausted before this row; re-send it in a smaller batch.

ResolveRow.description:
One row of a reconciliation batch. Every field is optional, but a row
with no identifier at all resolves to `not_covered` + `no_identifiers`
rather than failing the whole batch.

ref.description: Opaque client-supplied key, echoed back untouched so results can be joined to source rows. Must be unique within the batch if supplied. Results are also returned in input order.

cik.description: Accepted padded or bare: `CIK0000320193` and `320193` are equivalent.

ticker.description: Separator-insensitive: `BRK.B`, `BRK-B` and `BRK B` are equivalent. May carry the market as an ISO country suffix (`01316.HK`, `VOLV B.SE`, `PETR4.BR`): the ticker is then matched only against companies listed in that market.

name.description: Used to corroborate a ticker match, and as a last-resort candidate lookup. A name alone never produces a `matched` result.

exchange_name.description: Display name of the exchange, when the MIC maps to a known venue.

id.description: Unique identifier for the source. Filter filings with `?source=<id>`.

name.description: Generic label identifying the regional authority for this data source. Not unique: several sources can share a label, so use `id` to tell them apart.

url.description: Homepage URL for the data source, when available.

has_named_speakers.description: True if this source's call transcripts are confirmed to name each speaker (name, title, affiliation), false if they are confirmed to use generic labels such as 'Speaker 1', null if not yet measured. Treat null as unknown, not as false: an unmeasured source is not the same claim as a confirmed-generic one. Not meaningful for sources without transcripts.

X-Filing-Timestamp and X-Filing-Signature-256 are recomputed on every attempt at send time and appear here as placeholders, not as the values your endpoint received.

request_payload.description: Reconstructed request payload. Built dynamically from the referenced filing.

processing_status.description: The current processing status of the filing (e.g., 'PENDING', 'COMPLETED').

filing_type_code.description: Short code for the filing type (e.g., '10-K'). May be null for 'filing.received' events.

filing_type_name.description: Human-readable filing type (e.g., 'Annual Report'). May be null for 'filing.received' events.

language_code.description: ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., 'en'). May be null for 'filing.received' events.

language_name.description: Human-readable language name (e.g., 'English'). May be null for 'filing.received' events.

dissemination_datetime.description: The exact time the filing was disseminated by the source.

release_datetime.description: The official release time of the filing at the source.

ingestion_mode.description:
Whether the filing was added to the platform promptly after publication. `REALTIME`: added within the source's normal publication delay (5 to 48 hours after `release_datetime`, depending on the source). `BACKFILLED`: everything else, including historical imports and new filings that reached the platform late, for example after a source outage. Set once when the filing is added and not recalculated afterwards. Webhooks are not sent for filings added more than 48 hours after `release_datetime` (for a few sources, after `dissemination_datetime`; outside a recovery window we open after an outage on our side) unless the webhook has `deliver_late_filings` enabled, so most deliveries are REALTIME. A delivery can still carry BACKFILLED when the filing arrived after its source's normal delay but inside those 48 hours, has no `release_datetime`, falls in such a recovery window, or is a late delivery (`late: true`).

* `REALTIME` - Realtime
* `BACKFILLED` - Backfilled

fiscal_year.description: The accounting fiscal year this filing covers (e.g., 2024), as on GET /filings/{id}/. Null if not yet determined, which is common on 'filing.received'.

fiscal_period.description:
The fiscal period covered (FY, Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, H1, H2, 9M), as on GET /filings/{id}/. Null if not yet determined, which is common on 'filing.received'.

* `FY` - Full Year
* `Q1` - First Quarter
* `Q2` - Second Quarter
* `Q3` - Third Quarter
* `Q4` - Fourth Quarter
* `H1` - First Half
* `H2` - Second Half
* `9M` - Nine Months

period_ending_date.description: The date the reported financial period ends (YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2024-12-31), as on GET /filings/{id}/. Null if not yet determined.

updated_date.description: When the filing record was last modified (ISO 8601, UTC), as on GET /filings/{id}/. Taken when the payload is built, so a retry or replay can carry a later value than the first attempt.

late.description: True when the filing reached the platform more than 48 hours after publication. Such filings are sent only to webhooks with `deliver_late_filings` enabled, and only up to 30 days late; the one exception is a deliberate re-send after an outage on our side, which can reach every webhook at any lag. Always present.

ingest_lag_hours.description: Hours between publication (`release_datetime`, or for a few sources `dissemination_datetime`) and the filing reaching the platform, to one decimal. Null when the filing has no `release_datetime`. Negative when the source dates the filing in the future.

document_url.description: Direct link to our hosted copy of the original filing document (e.g. PDF). The link is not signed and does not expire: anyone holding it can download the file, so treat it like a share link. It returns 404 if the filing is later removed or its document replaced. Processed content is served differently: markdown requires an API key and HTML is served through short-lived signed links.

source_url.description: Original public link for the filing at the source authority. Null unless the webhook owner's account has source identities unlocked, the source is anonymised, or no stable link exists.

source_filing_type.description: The source authority's own classification label, verbatim. Null when the source publishes no label, it was not captured, or the source is anonymised. Not gated on source identities.

source.description: The same object as `source` on GET /filings/{id}/. Unless the webhook owner's account has source identities unlocked, `name` is a generic label and `url` is null; `id` is always the real source id (the manifests' `source_id`). Null when the filing has no source.

markdown_content.description: The full, processed content of the filing in Markdown format. This field is only included if your webhook is configured with 'include_markdown: true' and the event type is 'filing.processed'. It is null for 'filing.received'. Even with 'include_markdown: true' on a 'filing.processed' event, this field is null unless the webhook owner's plan includes filing markdown, the same check as GET /filings/{id}/markdown/.
